name: Zone of Pain (Rigid Core)
description: Instability (A) and abstractness (I) are both at or below 0.3 and the package holds at least 500 lines: the measured shape Martin calls the Zone of Pain. Interpreted as many concrete, stable classes that other packages depend on. Stability here is the measured afferent/efferent ratio, not observed change history.

name: Zone of Uselessness
description: Instability (A) and abstractness (I) are both at or above 0.7 with at least 3 abstract classes: the measured shape of the Zone of Uselessness. Interpreted as many abstract types that depend on things outside the package.

name: God Package (Blob)
description: At least 2000 lines, a maintainability index at or below 65, and Halstead volume at or above 100000.

name: Coupling Hub
description: Both efferent type (Ce) and afferent type (Ca) at or above 20. Interpreted as a package coupled in both directions at once.

name: Unstable Utility
description: At least 5 static utility classes and instability (I) at or above 0.7. Interpreted as a package whose types are called from elsewhere. The tool does not measure how often the package actually changes.

name: Overly Complex Implementation
description: Halstead effort (PACHEF) at or above 50000 and difficulty (PAHD) at or above 30.

name: Error-Prone Package
description: Halstead errors (PACHER) at or above 5, Halstead vocabulary (PACHVC) at or above 120 and at least 500 non-comment statements. Halstead’s potential-errors measure is a formula over operator and operand counts, not a count of defects found.

name: Interface Bloat
description: At least 10 interfaces and at most 3 concrete classes. The ratio is a measurement; the word over-engineering is an interpretation of it.

name: Hidden Technical Debt
description: Efferent type (Ce) at or above 15, Halstead difficulty (PAHD) at or above 25, and a maintainability index between 65 and 85. Interpreted as a middling index that does not by itself reveal the coupling behind it.

name: High Efferent Dependency
description: Efferent type (Ce) at or above 25 with afferent type (Ca) at or below 5. Interpreted as a package that depends on many others and is depended on by few.
